result.rationale: group.hbs renders members via `{{each member in members itemView="group-member"}}` with no itemController, so group_member.hbs ({{#unless automatic}}) evaluates `automatic` on the member (Discourse.User), not the group controller; the diff shows no `automatic` property on User, so the remove link renders for automatic groups, and removeMember's DELETE is rejected server-side (can_not_modify_automatic → 422) with no UI feedback in the shown code. The mechanism is verifiable from the diff, though Ember context resolution nuances leave slight uncertainty.

judged_text: The item view template tests {{#unless automatic}}, but the view is rendered with the member (Discourse.User) as its context via itemView="group-member" in group.hbs, so `automatic` resolves against the User object (which has no such property) and is always falsy — the remove link renders for members of automatic groups. On automatic groups (admins, etc.) every member row shows the 'x' remove control; an admin who clicks it gets a bootbox confirm, a DELETE that the server rejects with 422 can_not_modify_automatic, and no visible feedback that nothing happened.

adjudication.rationale: In `group_member.hbs`, the template explicitly references `member` (e.g. `{{member.username}}`), which indicates it is relying on the `{{#each member in members ...}}` block keyword, not on the item itself being the template context. Given that, `automatic` is not being looked up on the `Discourse.User` member object by necessity; it can resolve from the surrounding controller/view context (the admin group controller proxies the group model, which has `automatic`). The diff alone does not verify the claim that `automatic` will always be falsy and that the remove link will render for automatic groups.
